clue.text: Gold found in load, bringing chaos

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a mass is a large quantity or heap, like a load
OR is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A prospector strikes gold in a cartload and the camp descends into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold comes from heraldry and is a crossword staple; it sits inside MASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a bog, and figuratively a confused, entangling mess, so it stands for disorder and confusion.

clue.text: A little telescope rarely works

definitions.note: plural noun: opera is the plural of opus

indicators.note: only a small part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters tucked inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A grumble that a cheap small telescope seldom functions properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a verb about the telescope functioning, but it is the noun: opera is the Latin plural of opus, a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus means a composition, and its Latin plural is used for several artistic compositions together.

clue.text: Sweet thing entertained by a party a great deal

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in and held inside the host's home

blocks.note: a dance is a kind of party; 'a' is taken as written
a bun is a small sweet cake

explanation.surface: A sugary guest gets lavishly entertained at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' is a social event here, not a political group; the article 'a' stays as its own letter at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is a plentiful quantity, a noun phrase matching a large amount of something.

clue.text: Poles either side of a toilet in bar

indicators.note: two things on either side of something flank it, so they wrap around it

blocks.note: S and N are the south and north poles
a loo is British slang for a toilet; 'a' is taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes a pub where Polish customers stand either side of the gents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland, but it means the two magnetic or geographic poles, S and N. Loo is everyday British for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a bar, especially a lounge bar in a British pub or a Wild West drinking house.

clue.text: Meat-packing plant exposed

indicators.note: to pack something is to hold it inside, as a case holds its contents

blocks.note: a reed is a tall waterside plant
veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: An abattoir has been uncovered, perhaps by an undercover journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meat-packing plant' reads as one factory, but the hyphenated phrase splits: meat is packed inside a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Revealed and exposed are synonyms as past participles, both meaning uncovered or made known.

clue.text: Genius in test cricket, so fantastic

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are freed from their order

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A pundit praises a brilliant performance in a Test match as fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: Test cricket is the long international form of the game, but here the words are just fifteen letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It's not rocket science' marks something easy, so a rocket scientist is an idiom for a very clever person.

clue.text: Toxic love instant when overwhelmed by beauty

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed and swallowed up by what overwhelms it

blocks.note: Venus is the goddess of beauty and a byword for it
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a mo is a moment, short for moment

explanation.surface: A warning that falling for a beauty at first sight can be a poisonous romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Love meaning O comes from the tennis score; mo is British shorthand for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Venomous describes a creature that injects poison, so it is a close synonym for poisonous or harmful.

clue.text: Agent doffs cap for thesp

indicators.note: to doff a cap is to take off the hat, so the top of the word comes off

blocks.note: a factor is an agent who does business for another

explanation.surface: A theatrical agent politely raises a hat to a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the cap is the first letter, F, which is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesp is a jokey abbreviation of thespian, a stage performer, after Thespis, the legendary first Greek player.

clue.text: Moving 'ouse when heading north, Latino relocated

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading from bottom to top
relocated letters are moved to new places, so their order changes

blocks.note: house is home, and the apostrophe drops its H as in Cockney speech
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Latino family moves house, going north and dropping aitches along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ouse signals a dropped H, so the synonym loses its H too: 'OME, which is reversed upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving as an adjective means stirring the feelings, which is what an emotional scene or speech does.

clue.text: US politician gets on with landlord

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
a publican is the landlord of a British pub

explanation.surface: An American politician gets along well with the pub landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: RE in the sense 'on the subject of' is a staple; a publican is the person who runs a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A Republican is a member of one of the two major American parties, so an example of a US politician.

clue.text: Money back for puppet

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, from the end to the start

blocks.note: loot is slang for money

explanation.surface: A refund demanded for a faulty puppet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money back' sounds like a refund, but 'back' turns the money word around.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool can be a person manipulated by others, just as a puppet is controlled by strings.

clue.text: Fine part of speech, and so meaningful

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the last of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Praise for a speech that is elegant and full of meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of speech' looks like grammar (noun, verb), but it means a piece of the word speech and the words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome and fine both mean good-looking or generous, as in a handsome or fine sum of money.

clue.text: Bird's egg sheep rolled over

indicators.note: something rolled over is turned upside down, its order flipped

blocks.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A bird's egg has been knocked over by a sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole joined string is turned round, not just the sheep; 'Bird's' is the definition plus 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The martin is a small swallow-like songbird, such as the house martin, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Cross country, one having flown out

indicators.note: something that has flown out is no longer there, so it is removed

blocks.note: a European country
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An irritable country after one of its citizens has flown abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is the verb: to span is to cross over.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge spans a river by crossing it, so the verbs are synonyms meaning to extend across.

clue.text: First fundamental truth broadcast?

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a principle is a fundamental truth or rule

explanation.surface: A question whether the leading basic truth is being proclaimed.
explanation.walkthrough: Principle and its sound-twin are spelt differently but said the same; the clue wants the adjective spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal as an adjective means chief or most important, the same as first in rank.

clue.text: Filler or whitewash?

blocks.note: first meaning: material packed into a cushion, toy or roast bird
second meaning: a heavy defeat in sport, with the loser scoring nothing

explanation.walkthrough: Whitewash looks like paint or a cover-up, but in sport it is a crushing defeat, and stuffing is the British slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both padding packed inside something and a thrashing in a game or match.

clue.text: Honoured agent's embraced last

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a Fed is a US federal agent
the latter is the last of two

explanation.surface: Someone feels honoured because their agent has hugged them at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent's' is read as 'agent has'; FED is American slang for an FBI officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel flattered is to feel pleased and honoured by attention or praise, as a past participle.

clue.text: Old hat on lecturer, gone

indicators.note: in a down entry, being on something means sitting above it, so the first piece comes first

blocks.note: passé means out of date
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: An academic's old hat has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like headgear but is the idiom for outdated; the hat in the scene is not literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Passed on is a gentle euphemism for died, as gone is, both used in the past tense.

clue.text: Erudite types in retail, it being horrid

indicators.note: something horrid is unpleasant and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bookish people working in a shop find the experience awful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plural, matching the Latin plural ending of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are educated people with a strong interest in literature, the learned intellectual class.

clue.text: Friend, completely unknown

blocks.note: all means wholly, completely
Y is an algebraic unknown, like X and Z

explanation.surface: A friend who turns out to be a total stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: Mathematicians use x, y and z for unknowns, so any of them can stand for 'unknown'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone on your side, a supporter or partner, so it is a close synonym.

clue.text: Powerful horse, one not moving?

blocks.note: first meaning: a racehorse with the stamina for long distances
second meaning: someone who remains where they are

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, literal reading: a person who stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, a horse that keeps going over long races is called by this name, and literally it is one who remains.

clue.text: Tenor having scratched rear behind Toscanini's back – he foolishly went too far!

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
scratching means withdrawing, so the rear end is struck off
coming behind means following on after, so this piece goes second

blocks.note: Toscanini was a famous Italian conductor
Enrico Caruso was the celebrated Italian tenor

explanation.surface: An operatic anecdote: the conductor and an overreaching tenor who embarrassed himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' is a famous singer, not the voice; dropping his last letter and putting the conductor's final letter in front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew too close to the sun on wax wings, which melted, a byword for reckless overreaching.

clue.text: King, say, in possession of schoolkid?

blocks.note: first meaning: a sovereign, of whom a king is an example
second meaning: something a pupil keeps in a pencil case for drawing lines

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint, flagged by the question mark: an item a pupil owns.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a monarch who governs and a straight measuring strip used for drawing lines.

clue.text: Symbols in Old Testment grasped by people

indicators.note: something grasped is held in a hand, so it sits inside the holder

blocks.note: a nation is a people
the first letters of the two words, which name the Old Testament (misspelt in the clue)

explanation.surface: Signs found in scripture are understood by ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue misspells Testament; the abbreviation is unaffected.
explanation.definitionFit: A notation is a system of written signs, such as musical or mathematical marks, so it is a set of symbols.

clue.text: Speak of regret and the effect, first of all

indicators.note: the first of all the following words means each one's opening letter

blocks.note: initials of the five words

explanation.surface: Someone voices remorse and its consequences before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speak of' reads as one phrase, but 'of' belongs to the letters, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a formal speech, so it is a grander synonym for talking publicly.

clue.text: Dude found behind old stone

indicators.note: being behind means coming after, so the first piece named follows the second

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
dude is slang for a mate or pal

explanation.surface: A man is discovered lurking behind an ancient monolith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old stone' looks like a monument, but old is just its letter and stone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone with shifting rainbow colours, so it is an example of a precious stone.

clue.text: Newspaper produced includes article for basic pay

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it as part of the whole, so it goes within

blocks.note: a daily is a newspaper published every day
bred means produced, as offspring
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A paper's output includes a piece on the minimum wage.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, so the phrase from the Lord's Prayer has come to mean one's livelihood.
explanation.definitionFit: Daily bread means the essentials needed to live, and so the regular earnings that pay for them.

clue.text: Something musical in opening wine

indicators.note: an opening is a gap in something, so a piece is set into a gap made in another

blocks.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Music plays as a bottle is uncorked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening wine' looks like uncorking a bottle; here opening means making a gap, which the little word fills.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, so it is vaguely but fairly described as a musical thing.

clue.text: Looking from either side, it's more bloodshot

indicators.note: a word that reads the same from either side is the same backwards and forwards

blocks.note: the answer reads the same in both directions
the meaning the symmetrical word must also carry

explanation.surface: An eye examined from both sides is even more bloodshot.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase says only that the answer reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodshot eyes show red veins, so a more bloodshot eye is a deeper colour of red, a comparative.
